chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one with pockmarks and the one with the broken limb perform tayammum with dust when sexual impurity hits them.

key_terms.الْكَسِيرُ: the one with a broken limb
key_terms.الْمَجْدُورُ: the one with pockmarks (a specific type of skin condition/injury)

ai.seo_question: How do those with injuries perform ritual purification when they cannot use water?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific application of tayammum for those suffering from majdur (pockmarks) or kasir (broken limbs) who are unable to use water due to the risk of worsening their condition or pain. It highlights the Shia juristic principle of removing hardship (raf' al-haraj) by allowing dry ablution with earth when water usage is contraindicated, ensuring ritual purity remains accessible despite physical limitations. The ruling underscores the flexibility of fiqh in accommodating medical realities while maintaining the sanctity of purification rites.
